evals.prompt: I teach first-year cell biology. Can you make me one interactive figure that shows how ATP synthase makes ATP in mitochondria, the polished kind, as a single HTML file I can open in class? White background. I want students to see the protons turning the rotor and the ATP coming out.
evals.expected_output: A single standalone light HTML page with one textbook-style figure of mammalian ATP synthase in the inner mitochondrial membrane, drawn as a phospholipid bilayer of round heads and wavy tails, with the intermembrane space tinted above and the matrix tinted below. The c-ring has 8 subunits (bovine), F1 is three α and three β subunits alternating in two shades of one hue and faces the matrix, and the central stalk, a-subunit, peripheral stalk and OSCP are each colour-coded. Red flow arrows show protons entering the a-subunit from the intermembrane space and leaving into the matrix, a dark arrow shows the rotation (anticlockwise seen from the matrix), and ADP + Pi → ATP is written beside the head. The model is a pure module with named constants and a SOURCES list: 8 H+ and 3 ATP per turn, 45° proton steps with dwells, and a readout of protons, angle and ATP with the real rate and the playback speed. It looks like a figure from a good biology textbook (Campbell, Alberts, OpenStax) and nothing like an engineering drawing: no base plates, posts, screws, rulers, label plates, faceted four-tone shading, black hairlines or monochrome. Bodies are soft gradient-shaded shapes from kit/bio.mjs with outlines in a darker shade of their own colour, colours come from the palette and follow textbook conventions, compartments are tinted and named in spaced capitals, and short sentence-case labels with thin leader lines ending in dots name every part the caption mentions, set in clear space with no crossing leaders. The biology review (counts, direction, compartments, scale, sources) and the textbook review are written out, with screenshots in both themes and close-ups read.

evals.prompt: For a microbiology explainer on chemotaxis, make an interactive isometric figure of E. coli swimming: show the flagellar motor in the cell envelope and how switching rotation direction makes it run or tumble. evals.expected_output: A React TSX component (model and scene in plain .ts modules, the static figure in a server component, one 'use client' component redrawing the moving parts) and a standalone dark HTML preview, in textbook style. evals.prompt: For a lab methods tutorial, make an interactive textbook-style figure of agarose gel electrophoresis with a DNA ladder and three samples running. Show the bands separating by size when the power is on. One HTML file, light theme.
evals.expected_output: A single standalone light HTML page explaining agarose gel electrophoresis in textbook style: a simplified gel tank seen at an angle with buffer, the wells at the negative electrode (black) and the positive electrode (red) at the far end, a DNA ladder and three sample lanes, and an inset showing negatively charged DNA fragments moving through the agarose mesh.
